feedback:
The candidate changes one variable from the best raced design, iteration 6 (kp 6.5, kd 0.6, 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.030 m, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05, last_direction, score 122.66). kd goes from 0.6 to 0.5, and kp, geometry, base_speed, ki and line_loss stay the same. The rationale matches the evidence. Oval steering_oscillation has stayed between 0.250 and 0.270 across kd 0.4, 0.5 and 0.6 (iterations 3 to 6), so more kd has not reduced it, and the s-bend value rose with kd (0.238 at kd 0.6 in iteration 5). Oval max_error has stayed at 0.063 to 0.064, just over the 0.06 off-track limit, and body_width cannot relax that limit, so control must fix it. Line losses are still 1.3 on the oval, 1.6 on the s-bend and 1.0 on the slalom (iteration 6). Nothing here states how this candidate will perform. It is a low-risk, single-variable step, and with 4 iterations left after this one a raced result is more useful than another desk review, so approve it to race.

After the race, use the telemetry as follows. If oval steering_oscillation falls to about 0.2 or below while max_error stays at or below 0.063, keep kd 0.5 and test a wider array (x = ±0.040 m, 16 mm sensors) with kp near 8. If oscillation is still above 0.2 at kd 0.5 and kp 6.5, return kd to 0.6 and reduce kp toward 6.0 rather than adding damping. If max_error stays at or above 0.06 with oscillation low, widen the array as above. If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more at the same s-bend entries, test line_loss search_left or search_right, choosing the side the failing bends turn towards. Raise base_speed toward 1.6 only if progress is still below 1 with max_error under 0.06.
